experiment: Fixed 300032-step follow-up, five paired training seeds per family

gate_1.reason: The original supported-history construction still establishes decision relevance of earlier quote evidence. This follow-up does not estimate its prevalence on learned trajectories.

gate_2.reason: All five recurrent point estimates are below the predeclared fixed-wide reference. Seeds 11, 14 and 15 favor that quote almost independently of inputs; seed 13 concentrates on directional quoting and time-dependent abstention; seed 12 varies with inputs but performs worse than fixed quoting.
gate_2.limitation: Five-seed uncertainty is broad; failure to demonstrate a useful adaptive family is not proof that recurrence cannot learn.

gate_3.reason: Every recurrent seed underperforms both matched-budget current-observation and history-8 policies. Capacity and closed-loop memory channels differ, so this does not isolate a general causal effect of recurrence.

gate_4.reason: The recurrent behavior gate failed. The analysis cohort beginning at 6000000 remains unused. Existing smoke probes are implementation checks only.

next_experiment.controls: Five paired recurrent seeds, 300032 steps, gamma 1, entropy coefficient 0, unchanged architecture and economic objective; reevaluate both arms and fixed/history references on newly reserved episodes.
next_experiment.interpretation: Tests sensitivity to the advantage estimator. Terminal credit assignment and premature commitment remain hypotheses, not diagnosed causes.
